480	Allow me a moment to take this whole topic
481	down to the personal level as well.
482	Sukkot is a festival of very, very great joy.
483	The greatest joy is mentioned in the festival of Sukkot.
484	If we look at the verses of the Torah, on Pesach it doesn't say
485	"joy" at all, on Shavuot it is written once, and on Sukkot
486	it is written twice: "And you shall rejoice in your festival, you... He loved you," and so on,
487	"for HaShem your Elokim will bless you," and so on, "and you shall be only joyful."
488	"You shall rejoice in your festival... and you shall be only joyful."
489	Where does the great joy of Sukkot come from? There are
490	many angles on this, but one that I think is
491	very, very, very deep: what is the sukkah?
492	The sukkah is the point of trust in HaShem. The sukkah is
493	"the shade of faith." What is the shade of faith? It is
494	that you actually see — for this you must sit in a sukkah
495	that is under twenty cubits, so that you see the s'chach. For
496	the s'chach is an expression of the Clouds of Glory. Sukkot corresponds to
497	the Clouds of Glory. What are the Clouds of Glory? The cloud of HaShem
498	"And the pillar of cloud went and came between the camp of
499	Egypt and the camp of Israel, and there was the cloud and the darkness, and it lit
500	up the night, and one did not draw near the other" all night. The clouds are
501	a fortress of protection: "He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High, in the shade of Shakai he lodges."
502	That is, the sukkah: "And there shall be a sukkah for shade by day, for refuge
503	and for shelter from storm and rain." The sukkah is protection, a fortress
504	of protection. What is it really, the sukkah? It is a fortress, it is
505	a dwelling of the…
506	…once there was a war, rescuers…
507	there was fire from Gaza, I have many years, so
508	someone called me, someone said to me, "Rabbi, they are shooting
509	at us and we have no…" I said to him, "What do you have?
510	Where can you take cover?" "We have nothing, it's an open area." I said
511	to him, "What do you have? A sukkah." I told him, "Go into the sukkah."
512	The sukkah is protection. If you have no other place there,
513	of course, if there is a safe room or something, rely on that, not
514	on the sukkah — we don't rely on a miracle. But if there is
515	nothing else, then go into the sukkah. The sukkah is a fortress
516	of protection. Now what protection is there in the sukkah?
517	"So that your generations will know." When you know, when you live
518	with the awareness that HaShem leads us
519	and guides us, that itself gives a person
520	divine protection. Trust in HaShem causes
521	a person to be protected. Right? So it is written: "And he who trusts
522	in HaShem, kindness surrounds him." And when I am full of the awareness that HaShem
523	Yitbarach guides the world and there is none besides Him, and I am
524	permeated with this awareness, that very thing draws down upon
525	the person, as the Nefesh HaChaim writes, that it is a proven remedy,
526	that a person should be silent in the depth of his heart that HaShem
527	guides the world and there is none besides Him, and that itself
528	will protect the person greatly. The holy Zohar says, Rabbi
529	Shimon bar Yochai writes: "One who strengthens trust and
530	power in the Holy One, blessed be He, that is, who places
531	his trust and strength in the Holy One, blessed be He, does not fear
532	... all the people of the world; he is guarded and protected."
533	The power of trust in HaShem is an exceedingly great power.
534	And where does it begin? From that great awareness:
535	"So that your generations will know." So when a person lives
536	from the fact that HaShem Yitbarach sees — how does King David
537	say it? "HaShem is my shepherd, I shall not lack." "I shall not lack, for HaShem
538	is with me." "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me." "Even though I walk
539	through the valley of the shadow of death." Of course, this doesn't mean living in a pastoral idyll where
540	everything is always rosy. "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death,
541	I will fear no evil, for You are with me." "You are with me" doesn't only mean
542	that we are walking here inside some tanks
543	and RPGs and you are walking with the Holy One, blessed be He. There is
544	something deeper here. What it means is: I understand
545	that You, Master of the world, made this whole
546	reality, great and vast. I walk with You in everything,
547	because the whole world is an atmosphere of divine
548	presence. So King David walks through this, how many difficult
549	moments, walking with the kindness of song, with the justice of song.
550	This trust in the Holy One, blessed be He, brings a person
551	to great joy. And so, after you have purified your heart
552	during ten days of the work of that deep
553	unity, of "there is none besides Him," when you reach Yom Kippur
554	you cry out "Baruch shem kevod malchuto" aloud. For this is
555	no longer hidden, as if the kingship of HaShem were not revealed.
556	The kingship of HaShem is revealed and clear, that He is the only King.
557	When this shines within a person's heart, he is filled
558	with joy that comes from this great faith of those ten
559	days. When I then go out to life in Sukkot —
560	this is an expression of going out to life — if I go out
561	to life with the Master of the world, I am joyful, because I
562	know that even if I am competing in a tender against someone,
563	I know that in the end no person touches what is prepared
564	for his fellow. I will make every effort on the visible
565	level, I will prepare professional sketches, I will work
566	well, I will bring a proper business plan, I will consult with
567	people who understand, I will bring, I will invest,
568	at the level of effort I will do everything necessary, because
569	that is what the Holy One, blessed be He, wants from us. But I will
570	know in the depth of my heart that the Master of the world is directing
571	me, and I will arrive exactly at what is meant for me. I have
572	calm. I do not consume myself over the result. I do all
573	the effort, and the result is in the hands of the Holy One, blessed be
574	He. "The horse is readied for the day of battle, but victory is HaShem's,"
575	says Rabbenu Bachya in his introduction to Parashat Shelach Lecha.
576	"The horse is readied for the day of battle": you must prepare
577	the horse, but you know that the Master of the world
578	determines what will be in the end. "Victory is HaShem's." The same thing
579	Rabbenu Yonah says: "If HaShem does not guard the city, the watchman stays awake
580	in vain."
581	From here you can infer: if HaShem does guard the city, the watchman does not stay awake
582	in vain. That is, either way: if the Guardian is HaShem,
583	the watchman is superfluous; it should have said, why are you even
584	guarding? HaShem is guarding the city, not you. But that
585	is not what is written. If HaShem does not guard, then the watchman stays awake
586	in vain. But if HaShem does guard, then the watchman does not stay awake in vain,
587	for how does His guarding appear? Through the soldiers, through
588	the watchmen.
589	We must make the effort, but we will not slide into effort
590	in such a way that we build for ourselves a worldview as if this is the only thing that exists
591	here, and that's it, and everything depends on the boss, whether he accepts this,
592	and on my marketing, whether he succeeds in marketing
593	the products. No — I will do my part, but everything is in the hands of
594	Heaven, and this gives us calm, trust, and serenity,
595	because "he who walks in innocence walks securely," if the Holy One, blessed be He, will walk securely.
596	But in order for me to live a life of effort
597	out of a strong awareness of the existence of the Holy One, blessed be He,
